massaman-curry.name: Massaman curry
massaman-curry.summary: A rich, mildly spicy Thai curry blending Persian, Indian, and Malay spices with Thai ingredients, typically made with chicken, potatoes, and peanuts in coconut milk.

bird-s-eye-chili.name: Bird's eye chili
bird-s-eye-chili.summary: A chili pepper variety native to Mexico, cultivated widely across Southeast Asia and used extensively in many Asian cuisines.

sheikh-ahmad-nobleman-of-siam.name: Sheikh Ahmad Qomi
sheikh-ahmad-nobleman-of-siam.summary: A Persian-born merchant who settled in Thailand's Ayutthaya Kingdom in the early 17th century, rose to a powerful court office, and is regarded as the ancestor of the influential Bunnag family.

bunnag-family.name: Bunnag family
bunnag-family.summary: Siamese aristocratic clan of Mon-Persian descent, influential during the late Ayutthaya and early Rattanakosin periods and favored by Chakri monarchs.

ayutthaya-kingdom.name: Ayutthaya Kingdom
ayutthaya-kingdom.summary: A Thai kingdom centered on the city of Ayutthaya from 1351 to 1767, a major hub of international trade considered a precursor of modern Thailand.

david-thompson-chef.name: David Thompson
david-thompson-chef.summary: Australian chef and restaurateur known for Thai cuisine; his London restaurant Nahm was the first Thai restaurant to earn a Michelin star.

malacca-sultanate.name: Malacca Sultanate
malacca-sultanate.summary: Malay sultanate founded around 1400 that grew into a major Southeast Asian trading port and center of Islamic learning, until it fell to Portugal in 1511.

maritime-silk-road.name: Maritime Silk Road
maritime-silk-road.summary: Ancient maritime trade route across the Indian Ocean and western Pacific linking Southeast Asia, East Asia, South Asia, Arabia, East Africa and Europe, active from the 2nd century BCE to the 15th century CE.

djong.name: Jong
djong.summary: A type of sailing ship originating in Java, used by Javanese sailors for trade and occasionally war, ranging from about 40 to 2,000 tons; the English word 'junk' derives from its name.

khmer-krom.name: Khmer Krom
khmer-krom.summary: Ethnic Khmer people native to the Mekong Delta in southern Vietnam, recognized as one of Vietnam's fifty-four ethnic minorities and considered indigenous to that region.

hmong-people.name: Hmong people
hmong-people.summary: An ethnic group from East and Southeast Asia, based mainly in southwestern China, Vietnam, Laos, Thailand and Myanmar, with diaspora communities including in the United States and France.

kap-he-chom-khrueang-khao-wan.name: Kap He Chom Khrueang Khao Wan
kap-he-chom-khrueang-khao-wan.summary: A Thai poem written by King Rama II in 1800 praising savoury and sweet dishes, likely as an expression of love, and valued as a record of historical Thai cuisine.
kap-he-chom-khrueang-khao-wan.source_title: Kap He Chom Khrueang Khao Wan

rama-ii.name: Rama II
rama-ii.summary: Second king of Rattanakosin, Siam, ruling 1809 to 1824; his largely peaceful reign was a 'Golden Age' of literature, and he himself was a noted poet.

sri-suriyendra.name: Sri Suriyendra
sri-suriyendra.summary: Royal consort, later queen consort, of King Phutthaloetla Naphalai of Siam (1767–1836), and mother of the future kings Mongkut and Pinklao.

manila-galleon.name: Manila galleons
manila-galleon.summary: A Spanish trade route (1565–1815) linking the Philippines to Mexico across the Pacific, using galleons that made one or two round trips a year between Manila and Acapulco.

rice-terraces-of-the-philippine-cordille.name: Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras
rice-terraces-of-the-philippine-cordille.summary: A UNESCO World Heritage Site of rice terraces carved into the mountains of Luzon in the Philippines' Ifugao Province, the first cultural landscape ever listed, though studies suggest they date to about 400 years ago rather than 2,000.
rice-terraces-of-the-philippine-cordille.source_title: Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras

haw-phra-kaew.name: Haw Phra Kaew
haw-phra-kaew.summary: A former temple in Vientiane, Laos, built in 1565 to house the Emerald Buddha and rebuilt several times; it now holds a museum of religious art.

setthathirath.name: Setthathirath
setthathirath.summary: Ruler of the Lao kingdom of Lan Xang (1534-1571) who defended it against Burmese conqueror Bayinnaung and built major Buddhist monuments, including Wat Xieng Thong and the Pha That Luang.

monreal-stones.name: Monreal Stones
monreal-stones.summary: Two limestone tablets found on Ticao Island in the Philippines, carved with an archaic form of Visayan script, likely made no earlier than the 17th century.

arch-of-the-centuries.name: Arch of the Centuries
arch-of-the-centuries.summary: An arched gate at the University of Santo Tomas in Manila, half the surviving 17th-century original and half a 1954 replica, now a National Cultural Treasure.

our-lady-of-porta-vaga.name: Our Lady of Porta Vaga
our-lady-of-porta-vaga.summary: A Roman Catholic Marian title from a reported 1667 apparition to a Spanish soldier in the Philippines; her icon, the oldest dated Marian painting there, is enshrined in Cavite.

malacca.name: Malacca
malacca.summary: State in Malaysia on the Strait of Malacca whose capital, once seat of the Malacca Sultanate, was conquered by Portugal in 1511, ending its local monarchy.

tr-nh-nguy-n-war.name: Trịnh–Nguyễn War
tr-nh-nguy-n-war.summary: Prolonged 17th- to 18th-century civil war between the Trịnh lords of northern Vietnam and the Nguyễn lords of the south, ending in a long stalemate and a century of peace.

nguy-n-lords.name: Nguyễn lords
nguy-n-lords.summary: Feudal noble clan that ruled southern Vietnam (Đàng Trong) from 1558 to 1777 and 1780 to 1802 as forerunners of the Nguyễn dynasty, rivals of the northern Trịnh lords.

ng-trong.name: Đàng Trong
ng-trong.summary: The southern region of Vietnam under the Nguyễn lords from the 17th to 18th centuries, ruled as a de facto independent kingdom despite nominal loyalty to the Lê emperors.

tr-nh-lords.name: Trịnh lords
tr-nh-lords.summary: Feudal clan that were the de facto rulers of northern Vietnam (Tonkin) from 1545 to 1787, though formally subordinate to the Lê dynasty emperors.

ng-ngo-i.name: Đàng Ngoài
ng-ngo-i.summary: The northern region of Vietnam ruled by the Trịnh lords in the 17th and 18th centuries, with its capital at Thăng Long, now Hanoi; known to Europeans as Tonkin.

dutch-east-india-company.name: Dutch East India Company
dutch-east-india-company.summary: Dutch trading company founded in 1602 with a monopoly on Asian trade, holding quasi-governmental powers and considered by some the world's first multinational corporation.

sunda-kelapa.name: Sunda Kelapa
sunda-kelapa.summary: The old port of Jakarta at the mouth of the Ciliwung River, once the main port of the Sunda Kingdom; the Dutch seized it in 1619 and renamed it Batavia.

batavia-dutch-east-indies.name: Batavia
batavia-dutch-east-indies.summary: A Dutch colonial port city founded in 1619 on the site of Jayakarta, on the location of modern Jakarta, which served for about 320 years as capital of the Dutch East Indies.

ph-xu-n.name: Phú Xuân
ph-xu-n.summary: The historic capital of the Nguyễn lords and the Tây Sơn dynasty, later becoming the Nguyễn dynasty's capital under the name Huế.

tr-nh-t-c.name: Trịnh Tạc
tr-nh-t-c.summary: One of the most successful Trịnh lords, ruling northern Vietnam from 1657 to 1682; made peace with the Nguyễn and ended the last remnants of the Mạc dynasty.

tr-nh-t-ng.name: Trịnh Tùng
tr-nh-t-ng.summary: The de facto ruler of Đại Việt from 1572 to 1623 (1550–1623) and the first official Trịnh lord, under whom the war against the Mạc dynasty was successfully completed.

m-c-m-u-h-p.name: Mạc Mậu Hợp
m-c-m-u-h-p.summary: Fifth and effectively last reigning emperor of Vietnam's Mạc dynasty, ruling from 1562 to 1593.

fort-san-antonio-abad.name: Fort San Antonio Abad
fort-san-antonio-abad.summary: A Spanish fortification in Manila's Malate district, completed in 1584 during the Spanish colonial period.

fort-santiago.name: Fort Santiago
fort-santiago.summary: A citadel built in 1571 by Spanish governor Miguel López de Legazpi for Manila; Philippine hero José Rizal was imprisoned there before his 1896 execution.

m-c-dynasty.name: Mạc dynasty
m-c-dynasty.summary: A Vietnamese dynasty (1527–1677) that ruled all of Vietnam until 1540, then the north until 1593, surviving afterward in Cao Bằng under Chinese protection.

cao-b-ng-province.name: Cao Bằng province
cao-b-ng-province.summary: A province in northeastern Vietnam that borders China's Guangxi region.

m-c-ng-dung.name: Mạc Đăng Dung
m-c-ng-dung.summary: Founder of Vietnam's Mạc dynasty; a former imperial guard captain who rose to power and deposed the last Lê monarch to become emperor.

east-india-company.name: East India Company
east-india-company.summary: An English, later British, trading company founded in 1600 that grew to rule large parts of the Indian subcontinent, with its own armies, before dissolving in 1874.

josiah-child.name: Josiah Child
josiah-child.summary: English economist, merchant, and politician (c. 1630–1699) who championed mercantilism as governor of the East India Company and led it during the Anglo-Mughal War.

ch-n-m.name: Chữ Nôm
ch-n-m.summary: A complex writing system adapting Chinese characters to write vernacular Vietnamese, used mainly between the 15th and 19th centuries by literati such as Nguyễn Du.

ch-h-n.name: Chữ Hán
ch-h-n.summary: The Chinese characters used to write Literary Chinese and Sino-Vietnamese vocabulary in Vietnam, officially used from the Han dynasty's rule until the early 20th century.

vietnamese-alphabet.name: Vietnamese alphabet
vietnamese-alphabet.summary: The Latin-based writing system for Vietnamese, devised in the early 17th century by Portuguese missionary Francisco de Pina and other Jesuits, using diacritics to mark 29 letters and tones.

french-indochina.name: French Indochina
french-indochina.summary: A federation of French-ruled territories in Southeast Asia, including Vietnam, Cambodia and Laos, that existed from 1887 to 1954, with capitals at Hanoi and Saigon.

h-xu-n-h-ng.name: Hồ Xuân Hương
h-xu-n-h-ng.summary: Vietnamese poet (1772–1822) who wrote in the Nôm script during a turbulent era of rebellion and civil war, regarded as one of Vietnam's greatest classical poets.

l-qu-n.name: Lê Quý Đôn
l-qu-n.summary: 18th-century Vietnamese poet, encyclopedist and official (1726–1784), regarded as one of Vietnam's leading nationalist writers and a revered polymath for his prolific, wide-ranging work.

t-y-s-n-dynasty.name: Tây Sơn dynasty
t-y-s-n-dynasty.summary: Vietnamese dynasty founded by three peasant brothers who overthrew the ruling Trịnh and Nguyễn lords and the Lê dynasty, uniting Vietnam for the first time in 200 years before being replaced by the Nguyễn dynasty.

quang-trung.name: Nguyễn Huệ
quang-trung.summary: Also known as Emperor Quang Trung, second emperor of Vietnam's Tây Sơn dynasty (1788–1792) and a highly successful military commander who overthrew rival ruling houses.

nguy-n-dynasty.name: Nguyễn dynasty
nguy-n-dynasty.summary: The last Vietnamese dynasty, ruling unified Vietnam from 1802 until the French protectorate began in 1883, and nominally until 1945 when the last emperor abolished the treaty with France.

philippine-scripts.name: Suyat
philippine-scripts.summary: Proposed collective name for the indigenous Philippine writing systems, which developed from South Indian Brahmi scripts and flourished from around 300 BC.

university-of-santo-tomas-baybayin-docum.name: University of Santo Tomas Baybayin Documents
university-of-santo-tomas-baybayin-docum.summary: Two 17th-century land deeds written in the Baybayin script, declared a Philippine National Cultural Treasure in 2014 as the first paper documents to receive that status.
university-of-santo-tomas-baybayin-docum.source_title: University of Santo Tomas Baybayin Documents

i-vi-t.name: Đại Việt
i-vi-t.summary: The official name of several Vietnamese monarchies centered on modern Hanoi, first adopted as Đại Cồ Việt in 968 by Emperor Đinh Bộ Lĩnh. It lasted, mostly as Đại Việt, until 1804, when it was renamed Việt Nam.

l-m-c-war.name: Lê–Mạc War
l-m-c-war.summary: A civil war between Vietnam's Mạc and Revival Lê dynasties, fought from 1533 to 1592 during the Southern and Northern Dynasties period.

tom-pires.name: Tomé Pires
tom-pires.summary: Portuguese apothecary and diplomat (c. 1468–1524/1540) sent as ambassador to the Ming court, who never left China and wrote a major early description of Asian trade and geography.

cochinchina.name: Cochinchina
cochinchina.summary: Historical name for southern Vietnam, originally the Đàng Trong domain of the Nguyễn lords in the 17th-18th centuries, later a French colony from the 1860s.

l-chi-u-t-ng.name: Lê Chiêu Tông
l-chi-u-t-ng.summary: Emperor of Vietnam's Lê dynasty who reigned from 1516 to 1526 amid factional power struggles, before being killed by supporters of the general who seized power, Mạc Đăng Dung.

l-cung-ho-ng.name: Lê Cung Hoàng
l-cung-ho-ng.summary: The last emperor of the Later Lê dynasty of Vietnam, reigning from 1522 to 1527 before the dynasty's overthrow.

l-dynasty.name: Lê dynasty
l-dynasty.summary: The longest-ruling Vietnamese dynasty, governing Đại Việt from 1428 to 1789 (with a break from 1527–1533), founded by Lê Lợi after driving out Ming Chinese forces.

pierre-pigneau-de-b-haine.name: Pigneau de Behaine
pierre-pigneau-de-b-haine.summary: French Catholic bishop (1741–1799) best known for helping Nguyễn Ánh found the Nguyễn dynasty in Vietnam after the Tây Sơn rebellion.

gia-long.name: Gia Long
gia-long.summary: Born Nguyễn Phúc Ánh, he reunited Vietnam after civil war and became founding emperor of the Nguyễn dynasty in 1802, ruling until 1820.

lanfang-republic.name: Lanfang Republic
lanfang-republic.summary: A Kongsi republic in Western Borneo founded by the Hakka Chinese leader Luo Fangbo in 1777, lasting until Dutch occupation ended it in 1884.

west-kalimantan.name: West Kalimantan
west-kalimantan.summary: An Indonesian province on the island of Borneo, nicknamed the 'Province of a Thousand Rivers' for its many navigable waterways draining the Kapuas River basin.

kangxi-emperor.name: Kangxi Emperor
kangxi-emperor.summary: Third emperor of China's Qing dynasty (1654–1722), whose 61-year reign is the longest in Chinese history, who suppressed a revolt and expanded the empire into Taiwan and Tibet.

revolt-of-the-three-feudatories.name: Revolt of the Three Feudatories
revolt-of-the-three-feudatories.summary: A rebellion from 1673 to 1681 by three Han Chinese lords against the early Qing dynasty, ultimately defeated for lack of broader Han support.

m-c-k-nh-v.name: Mạc Kính Vũ
m-c-k-nh-v.summary: Tenth emperor of Vietnam's Mạc dynasty, reigning from 1638 to 1677, who fled to Qing China after being attacked by a Trịnh lord and died there in exile, no longer supported by the Qing.

yamada-nagamasa.name: Yamada Nagamasa
yamada-nagamasa.summary: Japanese adventurer (1590–1630) who rose to lead Ayutthaya's Japanese settlement and became governor of Nakhon Si Thammarat in what is now southern Thailand.

prasat-thong.name: Prasat Thong
prasat-thong.summary: Founder of the Prasat Thong dynasty who seized the throne of Siam's Ayutthaya Kingdom in 1629 and reigned until 1655, reasserting authority over Cambodia.

nakhon-si-thammarat.name: Nakhon Si Thammarat
nakhon-si-thammarat.summary: A city in southern Thailand that served as the administrative centre of the region for most of its history, originally on the coast before silting moved the shoreline.

hu.name: Huế
hu.summary: A city in central Vietnam that served as capital of Vietnam under the Nguyễn dynasty from 1802 to 1945, known today for its imperial palaces and tombs.

francis-light.name: Francis Light
francis-light.summary: British sailor and explorer (c. 1740–1794) who founded the British colony of Penang and its capital George Town in 1786; his son William Light later founded Adelaide.

george-town-penang.name: George Town, Penang
george-town-penang.summary: Capital of the Malaysian state of Penang, founded as a trading post by Francis Light in 1786 and now the commercial hub of northern Malaysia.

ottoman-caliphate.name: Ottoman Caliphate
ottoman-caliphate.summary: The Ottoman sultans' claim, from the 14th century on, to be caliphs of Islam, strengthened after they took Mecca, Medina and Jerusalem in 1517 and peaking under Abdul Hamid II.

tonkin.name: Tonkin
tonkin.summary: A historical name for the Red River Delta region of northern Vietnam, later used for the French colonial protectorate there from 1883 to 1945.

jesuits.name: Jesuits
jesuits.summary: A Catholic religious order founded in Rome in 1540 by Ignatius of Loyola, active worldwide in education, missionary work, charity and humanitarian efforts.

selangor.name: Selangor
selangor.summary: A state on the west coast of Peninsular Malaysia surrounding Kuala Lumpur, with the largest economy of any Malaysian state.

terengganu.name: Terengganu
terengganu.summary: A sultanate and state on the east coast of Peninsular Malaysia, known by the Arabic honorific 'Abode of Faith' and home to over 1.2 million people, mostly ethnic Malay-Muslims.

kalimantan.name: Kalimantan
kalimantan.summary: The Indonesian portion of the island of Borneo, making up about 73% of the island and comprising five Indonesian provinces.

sulawesi.name: Sulawesi
sulawesi.summary: Large island in Indonesia, also known as Celebes, lying east of Borneo and one of the country's most populous islands.

francesco-buzomi.name: Francesco Buzomi
francesco-buzomi.summary: Italian Jesuit missionary (1576–1639) and one of the first Catholic missionaries in Vietnam, helping lay the foundations of the Catholic Church there in the early 17th century.

north-maluku.name: North Moluccas
north-maluku.summary: Region covering the northern Maluku Islands of Indonesia, once home to the four largest Islamic sultanates in the eastern archipelago (Bacan, Jailolo, Tidore and Ternate), later contested by European powers.

ambon-island.name: Ambon
ambon-island.summary: An island in Indonesia's Maluku Islands whose main city, also called Ambon, is the capital of Maluku province.

alexandre-de-rhodes.name: Alexandre de Rhodes
alexandre-de-rhodes.summary: An Avignonese Jesuit missionary and lexicographer (1593–1660) who shaped Christianity in Vietnam and compiled the first Vietnamese-Portuguese-Latin dictionary in 1651.

o-m-u.name: Đạo Mẫu
o-m-u.summary: The worship of mother goddesses established in Vietnam in the 16th century, a more shamanic branch of Vietnamese folk religion honoring figures such as Princess Liễu Hạnh and the legendary Trưng Sisters.

anthony-reid-academic.name: Anthony Reid
anthony-reid-academic.summary: New Zealand-born historian of Southeast Asia (1939–2025), best known for his two-volume Southeast Asia in the Age of Commerce, exploring the region's material culture and social life.

sufism.name: Sufism
sufism.summary: An Islamic spiritual and ethical discipline concerned with purifying the self, closeness to God, and mystical experience, often described as Islamic mysticism.

abangan.name: Abangan
abangan.summary: Javanese Muslims who practice a syncretic form of Islam blending Hinduism, Buddhism and animism with local belief systems, unlike more orthodox Muslims.

fukuoka-prize.name: Fukuoka Prize
fukuoka-prize.summary: An award established in 1990 by the city of Fukuoka to honor individuals or organizations preserving or creating Asian culture, given annually in three categories.
